head: Weak
Stronger
rows: Academic writing is very difficult, and many people have different ideas about it.

Academic writing requires writers to coordinate disciplinary conventions, evidence, and audience expectations; these demands may be especially visible when students enter a new linguistic and institutional context.

02.key: Use interviews or focus groups for
head: Question-method mismatch
Better alignment
rows: How do first-year international students experience group work? A closed yes/no survey alone is unlikely to capture the process or meaning of that experience.
Use interviews or focus groups for detailed accounts, and add a survey only if the study also needs evidence about broader patterns.

03.key: Semi-structured interviews were appropriate because the
head: Untraceable claim
Traceable claim
rows: The method was appropriate, and the results were meaningful.

Semi-structured interviews were appropriate because the study examined how participants interpreted a shared institutional experience; the recurring accounts support a contextual, rather than universal, conclusion.

04.key: in one program describe access to academic advising
head: Unmanageable plan
Feasible plan
rows: Review all research on international students and determine the best policy for Korean universities.
Analyze how first-year international undergraduates in one program describe access to academic advising during their first semester.

05.key: Read the source, close it, state the idea from memory
head: Patchwriting
Ethical paraphrase process
rows: Students experience many academic and cultural challenges when they enter a new educational system.
Read the source, close it, state the idea from memory in relation to your argument, compare meanings, revise, and cite the source.

06.key: May I organize the body by
head: Vague request to a professor
Focused request
rows: Please tell me how to write this evaluation paper.
I understand that the paper must compare two theories. May I organize the body by criterion rather than discussing each theory separately?

head: Evidence without analysis
Synthesis
rows: Several studies reported difficulties. Kim (2021) found X. Lee (2020) found Y.
Across the studies, difficulties arose not from language alone but from the interaction of language, institutional access, and disciplinary expectations.

08.key: program interpret when and how to request advising
head: Topic only
Research problem
rows: This study is about international students in Korea.

Although universities provide academic support, little is known about how first-year international students in this program interpret when and how to request advising; this uncertainty may limit timely access to support.

head: Decorative theory
Integrated theory
rows: This study uses social identity theory. The next section describes the survey.
The survey measures identification, belonging, and boundary perception because these constructs operationalize the study's theoretical account of group membership.

10.key: access points - advising, mentoring, and orientation
head: Source-by-source reporting
Synthesis
rows: Kim studied advising. Lee studied mentoring. Park studied orientation.

Research on institutional support emphasizes three access points - advising, mentoring, and orientation - but the studies differ in whether students are treated as recipients of information or active interpreters of institutional norms.

11.key: defined population; this design estimates patterns of
head: Tool-centered justification
Methodological justification
rows: A survey was used because surveys are efficient.

A cross-sectional survey was selected because the study sought comparable self-reports across a defined population; this design estimates patterns of association but does not establish temporal or causal relationships.

12.key: lowest during the first month and increased after
head: Data dump
Analytical presentation
rows: Table 4 shows all responses. Many values are different.

As shown in Table 4, reported access to advising was lowest during the first month and increased after students attended departmental orientation; the pattern was strongest among first-semester undergraduates.

13.key: associated with clearer knowledge of advising routes
head: Overclaim
Proportional conclusion
rows: This study proves that orientation programs solve international students' academic problems.
Within the studied program, orientation was associated with clearer knowledge of advising routes; longitudinal research is needed to determine whether this knowledge improves later academic outcomes.

14.key: paragraph organization second, sentence style third
head: Late-stage editing error
Efficient sequence
rows: Correcting sentence style before confirming that the research questions match the analysis.
Review alignment and evidence first, section and paragraph organization second, sentence style third, and proofreading and formatting last.

15.key: the literature and methods needed to support
head: Thesis-to-article mistake
Audience-centered adaptation
rows: Submitting an entire thesis chapter with its full literature review and expecting journal editors to identify the contribution.
Select one article-level question, retain only the literature and methods needed to support it, and foreground the contribution expected by the target journal.

16.key: documented the data workflow, and presented the
head: Abstract skill claim
Evidence-based skill claim
rows: I have good research and communication skills.
I coordinated a multilingual interview study, documented the data workflow, and presented the analysis to both academic and practitioner audiences.
